summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of psoriatic arthritis, diabetes, morbid obesity, and a chronic left leg ulcer was admitted for recurrent cellulitis with worsening erythema, pain, and swelling near the wound site. He was started on broad-spectrum IV antibiotics due to leukocytosis and concern for deep infection. Imaging revealed new fluid and air collections in the left calf, prompting surgical consultation. After clinical deterioration, he underwent incision and drainage of a subcutaneous abscess. Antibiotics were narrowed to IV ceftriaxone based on infectious disease recommendation, and a PICC line was placed for outpatient therapy. His warfarin was held initially due to an elevated INR of 4.5 but was restarted at 10 mg daily, achieving therapeutic anticoagulation. Azathioprine was discontinued to support wound healing. The patient improved clinically, with resolving infection, stable diabetes control, and reduced pain. He was discharged home with a 14-day course of IV antibiotics, follow-up arranged in infectious disease, rheumatology, and plastic surgery, and detailed instructions on PICC line safety and warning signs.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
